The patient reports experiencing symptoms consistent with a major depressive episode. They have been feeling down for approximately three months following the loss of their job in July. The patient describes crying almost every day and a lack of enjoyment in activities they previously found pleasurable. Sleep disturbances are present, with the patient waking up at four in the morning and only managing about five hours of sleep per night. Appetite changes have also been noted, with a decrease in appetite leading to a weight loss of about ten pounds. The patient expresses occasional thoughts of not wanting to wake up, but denies having any plans to harm themselves or a history of self-harm attempts. There is no reported history of psychiatric hospitalizations, although the patient did see a therapist once during college. A family history of depression is noted, with the patient's mother having experienced depression, and an uncle with a history of heavy drinking. The patient reports no current use of alcohol or drugs, having stopped drinking a year ago. No allergies were reported by the patient.

The patient reports experiencing significant depressive symptoms for approximately three months following job loss, including daily crying and anhedonia. The patient also describes disrupted sleep, waking at four in the morning and achieving only about five hours of sleep per night, along with a decreased appetite and a weight loss of ten pounds. The patient expresses passive suicidal ideation, wishing not to wake up but denies any active suicidal intent or plans and has no history of self-harm.
paragraphs.evidence: I have been feeling really down for about three 3 months, since I lost my job in July. I cry almost every day and I do not enjoy anything anymore. I wake up at four 4 in the morning and cannot get back to sleep, so maybe five 5 hours a night. My appetite is bad and I lost about ten 10 pounds. Sometimes I wish I would not wake up, but I do not want to kill myself and I have no plan. I have never tried to hurt myself.

paragraphs.text: The provider identified these symptoms as indicative of a major depressive episode. The treatment plan proposed by the provider includes starting the patient on sertraline at a dose of fifty milligrams daily. The provider plans to follow up with the patient in two weeks. The provider decided against prescribing any sleeping pills or benzodiazepines at this time. The discussion included potential side effects of sertraline, such as nausea and headache, and considered the alternative of therapy only. The patient agreed to try sertraline.
paragraphs.evidence: I think this is a major depressive episode. I would like to start sertraline fifty 50 milligrams daily and I will see you again in two 2 weeks. I am not going to prescribe any sleeping pill or benzodiazepine today. We talked about side effects like nausea and headache, and the alternative of therapy only. Patient, okay, I would like to try the sertraline.
